calls.prompt:
Company: Brightside Foods Co.

US mid-size packaged food company (~900 employees, plants in Ohio and Georgia). Makes hot dogs and sausages, brightly colored gummy candy, and pecan-and-apple snack bars. Buys pecans, apples and corn from US farms. Sells through grocery chains and convenience stores (many customers pay with SNAP / food stamps). Runs its own fleet of 40 delivery trucks. No restaurants, no alcohol, no exports.

Rules that APPLY:
- FDA food additive and color additive rules (dyes in candy, casings, meat)
- Food labeling and food safety rules for packaged food and meat products
- EPA pesticide residue limits on crops we buy (pecans, apples, corn)
- USDA marketing orders and grading for pecans and apples
- SNAP rules that change what shoppers can buy or who qualifies (affects demand)
- Workplace safety and labor rules for food plants; trucking safety rules for our fleet

Rules that DO NOT apply:
- Aviation, airspace, aircraft airworthiness
- Banking, securities, crypto, sanctions
- Medicare/Medicaid payment rules, medical devices
- Mining, offshore oil and gas, fisheries
- Broadcast/TV licensing

Affected areas and owners:
- food-safety: Additives, dyes, labeling, food safety → Maria Chen (Food Safety & Regulatory)
- sourcing: Ingredients from farms, pesticide limits, crop rules → Tom Alvarez (Sourcing)
- sales: Retail channels, SNAP, pricing → Aisha Grant (Sales Compliance)
- operations: Plant safety, labor, trucking fleet → Ben Kowalski (Operations)

Task: Find every US Federal Register document published between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-13 (inclusive) that affects this company. For each, give the Federal Register document number, title, federalregister.gov URL, the key deadline, a tier (Critical if a deadline is < 90 days from 2026-11-13, otherwise High/Medium/Low by importance), the owner area, a one-line reason, and a one-line action. Only include items you found via search. Return an empty list if none.
calls.output:
I found 6 documents published 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-13 that affect Brightside. All 6 are Critical, because each has a deadline before 2027-02-11 (90 days after 2026-11-13).

My searches may not have caught every document in the window. I found no OSHA or FMCSA documents in the window that clearly apply to Brightside, and I found no FDA or FSIS labeling or food-safety documents.

## Items

**1. Document 2026-22866: Color Additive Petition From the International Association of Color Manufacturers; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Methylene Chloride, Trichloroethylene, and Ethylene Dichloride**
- URL: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22866/color-additive-petition-from-the-international-association-of-color-manufacturers-request-to-amend
- Published: 2026-11-10 (91 FR 72410). The document is a final rule.
- Key deadline: The orders are effective January 11, 2027. Comments on the notices are due December 12, 2026.
- Tier: **Critical**
- Owner: food-safety (Maria Chen)
- Reason: The rule removes the authorized use of three solvents for extracting annatto extract, paprika oleoresin, and turmeric oleoresin. These colors may be used in our hot dogs, sausages and gummies.
- Action: Ask color suppliers to confirm in writing that our annatto, paprika and turmeric colors are not made with these solvents, and that no inventory made with them is in our supply chain before 2027-01-11.

**2. Document 2026-22865: Color Additive Petition From Environmental Defense Fund et al.; Request To Amend the Color Additive Regulations To Remove the Solvents Ethylene Dichloride, Methylene Chloride, and Trichloroethylene**
- URL: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/10/2026-22865/color-additive-petition-from-environmental-defense-fund-et-al-request-to-amend-the-color-additive
- Published: 2026-11-10 (91 FR 72413). The document is a final rule (order).
- Key deadline: effective 2027-01-11, with comments due 2026-12-12, per the same reporting as item 1.
- Tier: **Critical** by the deadline rule. In practice the impact is likely small.
- Owner: food-safety (Maria Chen), with a copy to sourcing (Tom Alvarez)
- Reason: The order removes methylene chloride as a diluent in color additive mixtures in inks for marking fruit and vegetables. That could touch our apple supply. The remaining petition requests, on the extraction solvents, were denied.
- Action: Confirm with apple suppliers that none of their fruit-marking inks use methylene chloride.

**3. Document 2026-22936: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility**
- URL: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-22936. I built this short-form link from the document number. The search results did not show the full federalregister.gov address.
- Published: 2026-11-10 (91 FR 72454). The document is a proposed rule.
- Key deadline: Written comments must be received on or before December 10, 2026.
- Tier: **Critical**
- Owner: sales (Aisha Grant)
- Reason: The proposal would limit categorical eligibility to only households that receive TANF assistance. News coverage says the rule would reduce federal benefit spending by roughly $44.6 billion over five years. That likely lowers SNAP-funded demand at our grocery and convenience customers.
- Action: Model the SNAP sales exposure by channel and decide by 2026-12-10 whether to file comments, directly or through a trade association.

**4. Document 2026-22944: Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults**
- URL: https://www.federalregister.gov/d/2026-22944. I built this short-form link from the document number. The search results did not show the full federalregister.gov address.
- Published: 2026-11-10 (91 FR 72439). The document is a proposed rule.
- Key deadline: Written comments must be received on or before December 10, 2026.
- Tier: **Critical**
- Owner: sales (Aisha Grant)
- Reason: The rule would codify changes to the three-month SNAP time limit for certain participants subject to work requirements. This could change who qualifies, and therefore SNAP-driven demand.
- Action: Add this rule to the same SNAP demand analysis as item 3 and decide on comments by 2026-12-10.

**5. Document 2026-22826: Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas; Changes to Membership and Handling Requirements**
- URL: https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/09/2026-22826/pecans-grown-in-the-states-of-alabama-arkansas-arizona-california-florida-georgia-kansas-louisiana
- Published: 2026-11-09 (91 FR 70809). The document is a proposed rule from USDA's Agricultural Marketing Service (AMS).
- Key deadline: Written comments are due by Dec. 9, 2026
- Tier: **Critical**
- Owner: sourcing (Tom Alvarez)
- Reason: The proposal would change sheller membership on the American Pecan Council, adjust the inter-handler transfer report form, and add late fees and interest on unpaid assessments. Our pecan shellers and handlers are directly affected, which could change their costs and reporting.
- Action: Check whether Brightside or its pecan suppliers act as handlers under Order 986, and tell suppliers about the 2026-12-09 comment date.

## Documents reviewed and excluded
- **EPA ethephon tolerance, 2026-23120 (2026-11-13):** It establishes tolerances for ethephon residues in or on fig, which Brightside does not buy. I excluded it.
- **EPA isocycloseram emergency-exemption tolerance, 2026-23115 (2026-11-13):** The results did not show which crops it covers. The tolerance expires on December 31, 2029. Tom Alvarez may want to check the commodity list for pecans or corn.
- **SNAP stocking-standards 90-day extension (announced 2026-11-13):** USDA says By February 11, 2027, retailers must comply with the updated stocking standards. I found this as a USDA retailer notice, not a Federal Register document, so it is not on the list. It still matters for Aisha Grant's retail customers. The USDA FAQ says the new rule changes the classification of butter, jerky, cheese dip, snack bars, and fruit spreads. That could affect how our pecan-and-apple bars count at SNAP retailers.
- **FMCSA 2026-11-09 notice on driver exemption applications for epilepsy and seizure disorders:** It does not change the rules for our fleet, so I excluded it.

items.title: Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program: Reforming Categorical Eligibility
items.reason: This proposed rule (91 FR 72454, published 2026-11-10) would limit categorical eligibility to households receiving TANF assistance. News coverage says it would cut federal benefit spending by roughly $44.6 billion over five years, likely lowering SNAP-funded demand at our grocery and convenience customers.
items.action: Model the SNAP sales exposure by channel and decide by 2026-12-10 whether to file comments, directly or through a trade association.

items.title: Modification to Work Requirements for Able-Bodied Adults
items.reason: This proposed rule (91 FR 72439, published 2026-11-10) would codify changes to the three-month SNAP time limit for certain participants subject to work requirements. That could change who qualifies, and therefore SNAP-driven demand.
items.action: Add this rule to the same SNAP demand analysis as document 2026-22936 and decide on comments by 2026-12-10.

items.title: Pecans Grown in the States of Alabama, Arkansas, Arizona, California, Florida, Georgia, Kansas, Louisiana, Missouri, Mississippi, North Carolina, New Mexico, Oklahoma, South Carolina, and Texas; Changes to Membership and Handling Requirements
items.reason: This USDA AMS proposed rule (91 FR 70809, published 2026-11-09) would change sheller membership on the American Pecan Council, adjust the inter-handler transfer report form, and add late fees and interest on unpaid assessments. Our pecan shellers and handlers are directly affected, which could change their costs and reporting.
items.action: Check whether Brightside or its pecan suppliers act as handlers under Order 986, and tell suppliers about the 2026-12-09 comment date.
